newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - September 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Government considers building new harbour for Colombo, Shipping Minister M.H.M. Ashraff says. He says the Colombo port will not be able to handle the increasing workload in five years.
The government's peace proposals making progress through parliament, President Chandrika Kumaratunga tells CNN.
Deputy Finance Minister G. L. Peiris leaves Colombo to attend international finance ministers' meeting in Caribbean.
Sri Lanka marks International Ozone Day on Monday.
The Ceylon Workers Congress, a political party representing highland tea estate workers, ask government to grant citizenship to 150,000 Tamils of Indian origin, now working in the estates.
Government prepares to give big rewards in cash or land to those who provide information on the whereabouts of Tamil guerrilla leader Velupillai Prabhakaran, Police chief W.B. Rajaguru says.
Five soldiers killed in clash with Tamil rebels in the northern Jaffna peninsula.
Sri Lanka's majority Sinhalese community supports government's initiatives to end the 13-year old ethnic war, Kumaratunga tells a public rally.
